chunks: 4427 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Humran ibn A'yan:
Some of his family members wanted to marry, but he could not find a woman with whom he was satisfied, so that was mentioned to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, and he said:
"Where are you regarding the simple women and those who do not know anything?"
I said: "He only says that people are of two kinds: a disbeliever and a believer." So he said:
"Then where are those who mixed a righteous deed with another evil one, and where are those deferred for the command of Allah, that is, the pardon of Allah?"

key_terms.الْمُرْجَوْنَ: those left deferred or kept awaiting

ai.seo_question: Does this hadith allow marriage with someone who is not highly knowledgeable in religion?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses marriage and rejects a simplistic division of all people into only believers and disbelievers in practical social matters. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام cites Qur'anic categories of morally mixed or deferred persons, indicating recognition of people who are neither ideal nor outright outside consideration.
